title: Create a Mona webpage with Copilot CLI
subtitle: From a terminal prompt to a generated webpage and a connected web session.
purpose: Create a local animated HTML page using GitHub Copilot CLI, then access the same agent conversation through GitHub's web interface.

source.name: demo-ghc-cli.mp4
source.method: Selected video frames; visible actions and on-screen text only. Audio has not been transcribed.
source.note: This SOP documents the recorded demo, not a verified product-support statement. Timestamps identify sampled evidence, not exact action boundaries.

prerequisites: A Windows computer with GitHub Copilot CLI installed and authenticated. Installation and sign-in are not shown in the recording.
An approved local working folder where generating an HTML file is permitted.
A web browser and a GitHub account with the necessary Copilot access.
Permission to use remote session access under your organization's policies.
warnings: The recording enables all tool permissions and uses the user's home folder. Do not treat these demo choices as recommended practice: use a dedicated folder and least-privilege approvals.
Inspect generated HTML before opening it. Generated code and assistant claims require human verification.
Screenshots contain account and desktop context. Review and redact them before sharing outside the approved audience.
The final animation and mobile-access behavior have not been exhaustively tested. No process-owner approval is recorded.

steps.title: Confirm the working folder
steps.caption: Copilot CLI displays the folder-trust prompt.
steps.instruction: Start Copilot CLI in your approved working folder. Review the displayed path and confirm trust only if you recognize and trust the folder.
steps.expected: The interactive Copilot CLI prompt becomes available.
steps.caution: The recording starts with Copilot already open; the exact launch command is not visible. Avoid trusting an unnecessarily broad folder.

steps.title: Request the animated webpage
steps.caption: The natural-language request is submitted in the CLI.
steps.instruction: Enter the request below and allow Copilot to generate the HTML file, reviewing any requested permissions.
steps.command: create a static HTML web page, displaying an fun animation of Mona
steps.expected: Copilot begins creating a static page featuring Mona, GitHub's Octocat.

steps.title: Review the generated result
steps.caption: Copilot reports creating mona-animation.html and lists its features.
steps.instruction: Check that mona-animation.html has been created. Review the generated code and the assistant's description before opening the file.
steps.expected: The assistant lists floating motion, blinking eyes, animated tentacles, stars, bubbles, and click effects.
steps.caution: This screenshot establishes what Copilot reported, not that every animation or interaction works correctly.

steps.title: Open the HTML page
steps.caption: Windows offers a browser selection for the generated HTML file.
steps.instruction: Ask Copilot to open the generated file using the command below. If Windows asks which application to use, choose an approved browser.
steps.expected: The local HTML file opens in the selected browser.
steps.caution: Choosing a browser once is sufficient; changing the system default is not required.

steps.title: Enable remote session access
steps.caption: The CLI offers /remote on in its command suggestions.
steps.instruction: If remote access is allowed by your organization, return to the CLI and run /remote on.
steps.expected: Copilot establishes a remote connection and displays a session link.
steps.caution: This is an optional connectivity step, not a prerequisite for generating the local HTML page.

steps.title: Open the connected session link
steps.caption: The CLI reports that remote control is connected and shows a GitHub session URL.
steps.instruction: Open the GitHub session URL provided by your own CLI session. Authenticate if required by your organization.
steps.expected: GitHub opens the conversation associated with the running CLI session.
steps.caution: Use your own generated URL, not the personal session address visible in this recording.

steps.title: Check conversation continuity on the web
steps.caption: GitHub displays the same request, generated-file summary, and open-file command.
steps.instruction: Confirm that the web conversation contains the CLI request and response. Look for the remote-mode indicator before continuing the conversation.
steps.expected: The CLI conversation is visible in the GitHub web interface, with remote mode enabled.

steps.title: Inspect the generated webpage
steps.caption: The local page shows 'Meet Mona!' and a purple Octocat on a starry background.
steps.instruction: Switch to the local webpage tab and inspect the displayed result. Check animation and click effects manually before accepting the output.
steps.expected: The generated page displays Mona on a dark background with stars.
steps.caution: The screenshot confirms the visible design, but cannot prove animation timing or successful click behavior.

steps.title: Continue the conversation
steps.caption: A follow-up question and assistant response are visible in the connected web conversation.
steps.instruction: Use the web conversation for follow-up questions. The recording asks whether the session can also be accessed through GitHub Mobile.
steps.expected: The web interface displays the submitted question and an assistant response.
steps.caution: Mobile access is described by the assistant but not demonstrated. Validate supported versions and policies separately; do not mark mobile access as tested.
steps.evidence: Observed web exchange; mobile claim unverified
